[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.17] (3) On application by the applicant, the court may dispense with the need for the applicant to serve the evidence setting out a summary of the applicant’s financial resources on one or more of the parties. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.17] (4) The court may direct the applicant to provide additional information or evidence to support its application. ## Court to consider making directions

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > Court to consider making directions] 46.18 If the applicant is a body corporate, and the evidence supporting its application in accordance with rule 46.17(1)(b)(iv) sets out that it is unable to demonstrate that it is likely to have financial resources available to meet liabilities arising in connection with the proceedings, the court must consider giving directions for the provision of information about the applicant’s members and their ability to provide financial support for the purposes of the proceedings. ## Applications to vary judicial review costs capping orders

## 46.19

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.19] (1) An application to vary a judicial review costs capping order must be made on notice and, subject to paragraphs (2) and (3), in accordance with Part 23. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.19] (2) Subject to paragraph (3), the applicant must serve a copy of the application notice and copies of any supporting documents on every other party. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.19] (3) If the application is supported by evidence setting out a summary of the applicant’s financial resources, the court may, on application by the applicant, dispense with the need for the applicant to serve such evidence on one or more of the parties. ## VII SCALE COSTS FOR CLAIMS IN THE INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY ENTERPRISE COURT

## Scope and interpretation

## 46.20

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.20] (1) Subject to paragraph (2), this Section applies to proceedings in the Intellectual Property Enterprise Court. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.20] (2) This Section does not apply where—

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.20] (a)the court considers that a party has behaved in a manner which amounts to an abuse of the court’s process; or

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.20] (b)the claim concerns the infringement or revocation of a patent or registered design or registered trade mark the validity of which has been certified by a court or by the Comptroller-General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks in earlier proceedings. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.20] (3) The court will make a summary assessment of the costs of the party in whose favour any order for costs is made. Rules 44.2(8), 44.7(b) and Part 47 do not apply to this Section. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.20] (4) ‘Scale costs’ means the costs set out in Table A and Table B of the Practice Direction supplementing this Part. ## Amount of scale costs

## 46.21

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.21] (1) Subject to rule 46.22, the court will not order a party to pay total costs of more than—

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.21] (a)£60,000 on the final determination of a claim in relation to liability; and

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.21] (b)£30,000 on an inquiry as to damages or account of profits. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.21] (2) The amounts in paragraph (1) apply after the court has applied the provision on set off in accordance with rule 44.12(a). [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.21] (3) The maximum amount of scale costs that the court will award for each stage of the claim is set out in Practice Direction 46. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.21] (4) The amount of the scale costs awarded by the court in accordance with paragraph (3) will depend on the nature and complexity of the claim. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.21] (5) Subject to assessment where appropriate, the following may be recovered in addition to the amount of the scale costs set out in Practice Direction 46 – Costs – Special Cases—

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.21] (a)court fees;

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.21] (b)costs relating to the enforcement of any court order; and

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.21] (c)wasted costs. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.21] (6) Where appropriate, VAT may be recovered in addition to the amount of the scale costs and any reference in this Section to scale costs is a reference to those costs net of any such VAT. ## Summary assessment of the costs of an application where a party has behaved unreasonably

## 46.22

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.22] Costs awarded to a party under rule 63.26(2) are in addition to the total costs that may be awarded to that party under rule 46.21. ## SECTION VIII – ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW COSTS

## Environmental review costs

## 46.23

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.23] (1) In this Section, “party” includes an intervener or interested party. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.23] (2) Subject to paragraph (3), no party to a claim for environmental review (for which see Section III of Part 54) is entitled to an order for costs against any other party. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.23] (3) The court may make an order for costs against a party if satisfied that the conduct of a party or that party’s legal representative, before or during the proceedings, was unreasonable or improper. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.23] (4) Where—

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.23] (a)the court makes an order under paragraph (2) against a legally represented party; and

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.23] (b)the party is not present when the order is made,

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.23] the party’s legal representative must notify that party in writing of the order no later than 7 days after the legal representative receives notice of the order. ## SECTION IX Costs Limits in Aarhus Convention Claims

## Scope and interpretation

## 46.24

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.24] (1) This section provides for the costs which are to be recoverable between the parties in Aarhus Convention claims. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.24] (2) In this Section—

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.24] (a) “Aarhus Convention claim” means a claim brought by one or more members of the public by judicial review or review under statute which challenges the legality of any decision, act or omission of a body exercising public functions, and which is within the scope of Article 9(1), 9(2) or 9(3) of the UNECE Convention on Access to Information, Public Participation in Decision-Making and Access to Justice in Environmental Matters done at Aarhus, Denmark on 25 June 1998 (“the Aarhus Convention”);

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.24] (b) references to a member or members of the public are to be construed in accordance with the Aarhus Convention. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.24] (3) This Section does not apply to appeals other than appeals brought under section 289(1) of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990(1) or section 65(1) of the Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act 1990(2), which are for the purposes of this Section to be treated as reviews under statute. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.24] (Rule 52.19A makes provision in relation to costs of an appeal.)

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.24] (The Aarhus Convention is available on the UNECE website at https://www.unece.org/env/pp/welcome.html.)

## Opting out, and other cases where rules 46.26 to 46.28 do not apply to a claimant

## 46.25

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.25] (1) Subject to paragraph (2), rules 46.26 to 46.28 apply where a claimant who is a member of the public has—

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.25] (a) stated in the claim form that the claim is an Aarhus Convention claim; and

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.25] (b) filed and served with the claim form a schedule of the claimant’s financial resources, which is verified by a statement of truth and provides details of—

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.25] (i) the claimant’s significant assets, liabilities, income and expenditure; and

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.25] (ii) in relation to any financial support which any person has provided or is likely to provide to the claimant, the aggregate amount which has been provided and which is likely to be provided. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.25] (2) Subject to paragraph (3), rules 46.26 to 46.28 do not apply where the claimant has stated in the claim form that although the claim is an Aarhus Convention claim, the claimant does not wish those rules to apply. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.25] (3) If there is more than one claimant, rules 46.26 to 46.28 do not apply in relation to the costs payable by or to any claimant who has not acted as set out in paragraph (1), or who has acted as set out in paragraph (2), or who is not a member of the public. ## Limit on costs recoverable from a party in an Aarhus Convention claim

## 46.26

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.26] (1) Subject to rules 46.25 and 46.28, a claimant or defendant in an Aarhus Convention claim may not be ordered to pay costs exceeding the amounts in paragraph (2) or (3) or as varied in accordance with rule 46.27. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.26] (2) For a claimant the amount is—

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.26] (a )£5,000 where the claimant is claiming only as an individual and not as, or on behalf of, a business or other legal person;

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.26] (b) £10,000 in all other cases. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.26] (3) For a defendant the amount is £35,000. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.26] (4) In an Aarhus Convention claim with multiple claimants or multiple defendants, the amounts in paragraphs (2) and (3) (subject to any direction of the court under rule 46.27) apply in relation to each such claimant or defendant individually and may not be exceeded, irrespective of the number of receiving parties. ## Varying the limit on costs recoverable from a party in an Aarhus Convention claim

## 46.27

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.27] (1) The court may vary the amounts in rule 46.26 or may remove altogether the limits on the maximum costs liability of any party in an Aarhus Convention claim. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.27] (2) The court may vary such an amount or remove such a limit only on an application made in accordance with paragraphs (5) to (7) (“an application to vary”) and if satisfied that—

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.27] (a) to do so would not make the costs of the proceedings prohibitively expensive for the claimant; and

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.27] (b) in the case of a variation which would reduce a claimant’s maximum costs liability or increase that of a defendant, without the variation the costs of the proceedings would be prohibitively expensive for the claimant. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.27] (3) Proceedings are to be considered prohibitively expensive for the purpose of this rule if their likely costs (including any court fees which are payable by the claimant) either—

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.27] (a) exceed the financial resources of the claimant; or

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.27] (b) are objectively unreasonable having regard to—

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.27] (i) the situation of the parties;

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.27] (ii) whether the claimant has a reasonable prospect of success;

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.27] (iii) the importance of what is at stake for the claimant;

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.27] (iv) the importance of what is at stake for the environment;

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.27] (v) the complexity of the relevant law and procedure; and

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.27] (vi) whether the claim is frivolous. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.27] (4) When the court considers the financial resources of the claimant for the purposes of this rule, it must have regard to any financial support which any person has provided or is likely to provide to the claimant. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.27] (5) Subject to paragraph (6), an application to vary must—

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.27] (a) if made by the claimant, be made in the claim form and provide the claimant’s reasons why, if the variation were not made, the costs of the proceedings would be prohibitively expensive for the claimant;

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.27] (b) if made by the defendant, be made in the acknowledgment of service and provide the defendant’s reasons why, if the variation were made, the costs of the proceedings would not be prohibitively expensive for the claimant; and

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.27] (c) be determined by the court at the earliest opportunity. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.27] (6) An application to vary may be made at a later stage if there has been a significant change in circumstances (including evidence that the schedule of the claimant’s financial resources contained false or misleading information) which means that the proceedings would now—

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.27] (a) be prohibitively expensive for the claimant if the variation were not made; or

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.27] (b) not be prohibitively expensive for the claimant if the variation were made. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.27] (7) An application under paragraph (6) must—

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.27] (a) if made by the claimant—

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.27] (i) be accompanied by a revised schedule of the claimant’s financial resources or confirmation that the claimant’s financial resources have not changed; and

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.27] (ii) provide reasons why the proceedings would now be prohibitively expensive for the claimant if the variation were not made; and

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.27] (b) if made by the defendant, provide reasons why the proceedings would now not be prohibitively expensive for the claimant if the variation were made. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.27] (Rule 39.2(3)(c) makes provision for a hearing (or any part of it) to be in private if it involves confidential information (including information relating to personal financial matters) and publicity would damage that confidentiality.)

## Challenging whether the claim is an Aarhus Convention claim

## 46.28

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.28] (1) Where a claimant has complied with rule 46.25(1), and subject to rule 46.25(2) and (3), rule 46.26 applies unless—

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.28] (a )the defendant has in the acknowledgment of service—

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.28] (i) denied that the claim is an Aarhus Convention claim; and

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.28] (ii) set out the defendant’s grounds for such denial; and

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.28] (b) the court has determined that the claim is not an Aarhus Convention claim. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.28] (2) Where the defendant denies that the claim is an Aarhus Convention claim, the court must determine that issue at the earliest opportunity. [PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.28] (3) In any proceedings to determine whether the claim is an Aarhus Convention claim—

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.28] (a) if the court holds that the claim is not an Aarhus Convention claim, it shall, except for good reason, make no order for costs in relation to those proceedings;

[PART 46 – COSTS-SPECIAL CASES > 46.28] (b) if the court holds that the claim is an Aarhus Convention claim, it shall, except for good reason, order the defendant to pay the claimant’s costs of those proceedings to be assessed on the standard basis, and that order may be enforced even if this would increase the costs payable by the defendant beyond the amount stated in rule 46.26(3) or any variation of that amount. ## Footnotes
